geometry_edits.rationale: Split the compact mass into a clearer wing-and-void condition so the access edge can become a real threshold rather than a sealed object.
Use the principal axis to organize the split in the direction that can expose a frontage court.
Introduce a modest gap that reads as usable public void rather than a decorative notch.
Keep the composition grounded with a legible base element so the upper gesture does not float away from neighborhood use.

graph_edits.rationale: Convert the primary mass from a generic courtyard label into an explicit carved void so the street edge can become legible and public.
Size the void to be meaningfully occupiable while preserving a dominant compact mass.
Align the opening to the verified site-access side so the public threshold addresses the street frontage rather than turning inward.
Retain the upper hierarchy but make the connector read as a terrace/entry link that reinforces the public void instead of a vague appendage.
Pull the terrace link closer to the ground to strengthen the active threshold and sectional legibility.
Bind the connector to the street-facing side to clarify access and public entry.

rationale: The candidate reads coherently in volume but fails the program contract as a neighborhood-living mass: it is predominantly a compact stacked object with only a weak/ambiguous public void and a poor response to the verified access edge. Across the four views the silhouette is understandable, but the dominant gesture is too box-like and too internally concentrated to clearly support an active street threshold plus one meaningful shared court/terrace. The blue frontage is not met by a legible entry seam or carved public ground condition; instead the mass appears largely sealed or semantically opposite to the access edge. The stepped upper form is not disastrous, but it functions more as arbitrary tiering than as a capacity-bearing inhabited section. Reference 1 supports the idea of connected low-rise masses around a clear communal void and terrace ribbon, while reference 2 supports compact pavilion-like calmness with a readable ground edge; neither is fully matched, but both suggest the candidate should open and organize its base more deliberately.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This reference is more campus/community-center than compact neighborhood living; it is larger and more dispersed than the candidate should become.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Low-rise massing organized around a legible shared void, with connected wings and terrace-like section changes that keep the composition civic and walkable.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: It is too pavilion-like and single-story to be copied directly for a 5-floor neighborhood program; use only the threshold and proportion cues.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Simple pavilion logic with a clear ground-edge response, compact bar-like massing, and a small vertical accent that does not overwhelm the primary volume.

warnings: Parcel containment appears satisfied visually, but the access-edge response is insufficiently public.
The mass is coherent, but the ground relationship does not yet read as active neighborhood frontage.
Do not treat the stepped upper silhouette as programmatic evidence by itself.
